title: Chat stream readiness failure bypasses handlers.onError: the send promise rejects unhandled, the assistant message stays 'streaming' forever, Stop does nothing and later prompts queue behind it
repro: State: the shared readiness probe is not resolved when the user sends, i.e. boot landed in sidecarStatus='error' (120 s budget lapsed) or Rust reported port 0. Pick a keyed provider (Anthropic/OpenAI; the keyless path pre-checks via validateProvider) and send a prompt. streamAgentInvocation/streamChat await getSidecarBaseUrl() OUTSIDE consumeSseStream's try, so after the re-armed 120 s probe the SidecarError rejects the call without ever calling handlers.onError. Proof (vitest, getSidecarBaseUrl mocked to reject): 'P1 agent: onError calls = 0 | rejected with: The data engine did not become ready in time.' and the same rejection for streamChat. In ChatSidebar the call is `await streamAgentInvocation(...)` inside handleSend with no try, invoked as `void handleSend(text)`, so the rejection is unhandled after beginAssistant already set pending:true + streamingMessageId.
evidence: src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:134, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:153 (await getSidecarBaseUrl() before consumeSseStream), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:204-215 (the only try, which covers fetch only), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:114-144 (re-arms a fresh 120 s probe after a failure, then throws SidecarError 503), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:868-886 (beginAssistant + abortRef + startRun before the call), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1005-1038 (await with no try/catch), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1285-1297 (onSend queues while streamingMessageId !== null; onStop only aborts the controller), src/store/chat-history.ts:141-157 (beginAssistantMessage sets pending + streamingMessageId), docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof.test.ts.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof-output.txt
notes: Error-boundary drawn one await too late: the StreamingHandlers contract is 'failures arrive via onError', but one of the three awaits a stream call makes sits outside the try. Consequence: the assistant bubble spins for 120 s and then never settles; the composer stays in streaming mode, every later prompt is queued behind a stream that will never end (queue drain waits on streamingMessageId), the Stop square aborts a controller nothing listens to (getSidecarBaseUrl takes no signal), the rail run stays 'running' and a research brief stays in_flight. Only a thread switch or reload clears it. It fires exactly in the degraded states findings 12 and 14 (original raw) already describe, turning 'engine did not start' into 'chat is wedged'. Smallest fix: move the base-URL await inside consumeSseStream's try (pass the path, not a URL) so every pre-stream failure lands in onError; belt: wrap handleSend's stream call in try/catch that fails the message and ends the run.

title: Keyless first run with Ollama running but the default model not pulled: the gate passes, then the 404 'try pulling it first' is humanised to 'pick another model in Settings' and the onboarding pull flow is never offered
repro: Fresh Ollama install (daemon running, no models pulled), provider = Ollama, default model qwen2.5:7b. validateProvider -> /llm/keys/validate -> OllamaAdapter.validate_key only calls client.list(), which succeeds with an empty list -> ok:true, so onboarding is NOT opened. The chat call raises ollama.ResponseError(404, 'model "qwen2.5:7b" not found, try pulling it first'); humanize maps every 404 to model_not_found. Probe: humanize('ollama', ollama.ResponseError('model "qwen3:8b" not found, try pulling it first', 404)) -> message='The requested model is not available on Ollama — pick another model.', action='Choose a different model in Settings.'.
evidence: sidecar/services/errors.py:173-180 (404 -> 'pick another model' regardless of provider), sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:180-185 (ResponseError humanised with no model-pull special case), sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:237-246 (validate_key = daemon reachable, not model present), src/lib/sidecar-client.ts:218-243 (validateProvider doc: gate exists so a keyless provider never 'silently fails against an absent local model'), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:796-806 (onboarding opens only when validate fails), src/components/OnboardingFlow.tsx:490-502,600-601 (the pull flow that fixes exactly this), src/store/model-selection.ts:31 (ollama default 'qwen2.5:7b'), docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof-output.txt
notes: Special-general mixture again: humanize carries DeepSeek-specific 402 copy twice but has no row for the single most common local-first failure. The owner's zero-config first impression dead-ends: the Settings model picker's live Ollama list is empty (nothing pulled), so 'choose a different model' has nothing to choose, while the app already ships a working 'Download model' flow it never routes to. Distinct from original finding 5 (that covers a STOPPED daemon); here the daemon is up. Smallest fix: in humanize, provider=='ollama' and 404 with 'not found'/'pull' in the text -> code='model_not_pulled', message 'The model <x> is not downloaded yet', action 'Download it in setup'; ChatSidebar opens onboarding on that code. Better: validate_key for ollama also checks the selected model is in list().

title: A truncated answer (finish_reason max_tokens/length) is shown as a complete one: every adapter reports it, streaming.ts parses it, ChatSidebar drops it, and Anthropic is hard-capped at 4096 output tokens
repro: design + code trace: an Anthropic turn whose answer exceeds DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 (nothing on the agent/chat path raises it) ends with stop_reason 'max_tokens'; the adapter yields LLMDoneEvent(finish_reason='max_tokens'). OpenAI/Groq/Gemini/Ollama likewise carry 'length'. normalizeEvent maps it to event.finishReason, but makeHandlers' done branch passes only usage to onDone, and agent_runtime special-cases only 'content_filter'. The bubble finalises normally, mid-sentence or mid-table, with no notice.
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:36-37 (DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4_096), sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:110 and :142-146 (stop_reason forwarded as finish_reason), sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:785-787, sidecar/services/llm/groq.py:166-168,184, sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:216-218, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1485-1495 (only content_filter becomes an error frame), src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:338-342 (finishReason parsed), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:2025-2030 (done -> onDone(usage) only; finishReason discarded)
notes: A failure mode the error layer never names: 'the model ran out of room' is information the wire already carries and the UI throws away, so a cut-off research answer (the product's core artifact) reads as the model's complete view. The layer built the exact precedent for this (the content_filter notice) and stopped there. Smallest fix: in agent_runtime next to the content_filter branch, a length/max_tokens finish yields a notice (or the frontend onDone takes finishReason and marks the message 'truncated' with a 'Continue' affordance); raise Anthropic's default cap for the chat path.

title: Invalid-key failures that arrive as HTTP 400 (Gemini, xAI) are classified 'unknown': 'Something went wrong… Try again or switch provider'
repro: Live: POST generativelanguage.googleapis.com …:generateContent with a bogus key -> HTTP 400 {status:'INVALID_ARGUMENT', reason:'API_KEY_INVALID', message:'API key not valid…'}; POST api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions with a bogus key -> HTTP 400 {error:'Incorrect API key provided…'}. humanize('gemini', genai ClientError(400, that body)) -> code=unknown 'Something went wrong with Google Gemini.'; humanize('xai', openai.BadRequestError(400, that body)) -> code=unknown 'Something went wrong with xAI.'.
evidence: sidecar/services/errors.py:148-196 (status branches 402/401/403/404/429/5xx only; 400 falls through), sidecar/services/errors.py:253-260 (auth detected by CLASS name only, and ClientError/BadRequestError match nothing), sidecar/services/errors.py:295-300 (fallback), sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:198-202 (validate_key likewise treats only 401/403 as a bad key and re-raises the 400), docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/error-layer-2-proof-output.txt
notes: The status table encodes an OpenAI-shaped assumption (bad key = 401) that two supported providers do not follow. A rotated/revoked Gemini or xAI key produces advice to retry, which cannot succeed; the true cause is only behind the Details toggle. Low because entry-time validation catches most typos (though gemini validate_key re-raises the 400 as a 'transport error', see llm-adapters). Smallest fix: before the fallback, a body-text row: status 400 and ('api key not valid'|'api_key_invalid'|'incorrect api key') -> code='auth'; add both provider bodies as test_errors.py fixtures.
